memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If the defiling mould reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house scraped and plastered, the priest is to go and examine it and, if the mould has spread in the house, it is a persistent defiling mould; the house is unclean. It must be torn down — its stones, timbers and all the plaster — and taken out of the town to an unclean place." - Lev 14:43-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything was tried. Stones replaced, walls scraped, fresh plaster applied. And it came back. So the house comes down — stones, timbers, plaster, all of it carried away.

This is hard reading, and we should not soften it. Sometimes the answer is not repair.

There are situations in life where God's people have to face this. A business built on practices that cannot be made honest. A pattern of living that cannot be adjusted, only abandoned. Occasionally a plan we have poured years into, which has to be laid down.

The instinct is always to try one more repair. Surely a little more effort? But there comes a point where holding on to the structure costs more than losing it. Better to lose the house than to lose the family living in it.

And here is our hope. Jesus told of the wise builder whose house stood because it was built on rock (Matt 7:24-25). If a structure in your life has come down, it does not mean God has finished with you. It may mean He is rebuilding on better ground.

We have an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands (2 Cor 5:1). That one will never come down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you keep repairing that may need to be laid down?
2. What are you afraid of losing if you let it go?
3. What is your life actually built on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me wisdom to know what to repair and what to release. Where something must come down, build me again on the solid ground of Christ. Amen.
